papers.title: sortscore: Sort-seq MAVE scoring and visualization using Python
papers.summary: Abstract Summary A growing number of tools enable the analysis of large variant libraries produced by multiplexed assays of variant effects (MAVEs). Experiments using fluorescent reporters and fluorescence-activated cell sorting sequencing (FACS-seq or Sort-seq) can coarsely quantify a given variant's impact on phenotypes such as transcription activity. Existing bioinformatics tools for Sort-seq data broadly fall into two categories: methods that model a genotype-phenotype landscape to infer latent variant phenotypes, and methods that directly estimate individual variant scores from experimental binned counts. Within this second category, sortscore provides an activity score computed directly from observed counts without fitting a model, retaining the original experimental scale when bin median values are known.We present sortscore, a python package that incorporates a standard Sort-seq scoring method and normalization across sorted samples, technical replicates from separate sort times, and across oligos in tiled experiments. It also provides convenient heatmap visualizations. This software was used to analyze DMS experiments for the transcription factor GLI2. This work seeks to lower the barrier to entry and provide a clear starting point for scoring Sort-seq cell-based functional assays. This extends the availability of well-documented and reproducible data analysis protocols to a wider community employing MAVE techniques. Availability and Implementation The package can be downloaded from PyPI using the pip installer. The code is also freely accessible and available for reuse through a Public GitHub repository (MIT License). Installation instructions, documentation, and tutorials are accessible at the sortscore GitHub repository: https://github.com/dbaldridge-lab/sortscore . A snapshot of the code and data is available on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22119031

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 摘要：越来越多的工具能够帮助分析通过多重测序技术生成的庞大变异库。
llm_highlights_zh: 利用荧光报告基因及荧光激活细胞分选测序技术（FACS-seq或Sort-seq）进行的实验，能够大致量化特定变异对转录活性等表型特征的影响程度。
现有的用于处理Sort-seq数据的生物信息学工具大致可分为两类：一类是那些通过构建基因型-表型关系模型来推断潜在变异体所对应的表型特征的方法；另一类则是直接根据实验中获得的分箱计数结果来计算各个变异体的具体得分的方法。
在这第二类方法中，sortscore提供了一种直接根据观测数据计算得出的活动性评分方法——该方法无需建立任何模型进行数据分析，且当已知各分组的中位数值时，能够保留原始的实验测量尺度。我们推出的sortscore是一个Python软件包，它整合了标准的Sort-seq评分算法，并实现了对已排序样本、不同排序时间下获得的重复实验数据，以及分块实验中使用的各种寡核苷酸序列进行标准化处理的功能。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
摘要：越来越多的工具能够帮助分析通过多重测序技术产生的大量变异数据。利用荧光报告基因及荧光激活细胞分选测序技术，可以大致量化特定变异对转录活性等表型特征的影响。目前用于处理Sort-seq数据的生物信息学工具主要分为两类：一类是通过建立基因型-表型模型来推断潜在的变异效应；另一类则是直接根据实验结果计算各个变异的得分。在这第二类工具中，sortscore是一种无需建立模型即可根据观测数据直接计算变异活性的工具——当已知数据分组的中间值时，该工具能够保留原始的实验测量尺度。我们开发的sortscore是一个Python软件包，它包含了标准的Sort-seq评分方法，并能对不同时间进行的分选实验结果、重复实验数据以及嵌套实验中的多种寡核苷酸序列数据进行标准化处理；同时，它还提供了便捷的热图可视化功能。该工具已被用于分析GLI2转录因子的相关实验数据。我们的目标是降低使用Sort-seq技术进行细胞功能分析的门槛，为相关研究提供可靠的起点与方法支持，从而让更多采用多重测序技术的科研人员能够方便地利用这些经过充分验证的数据分析流程。

papers.primary_summary_raw:
SUMMARY: A growing number of tools enable the analysis of large variant libraries produced by multiplexed assays of variant effects (MAVEs). Experiments using fluorescent reporters and fluorescence-activated cell sorting sequencing (FACS-seq or Sort-seq) can coarsely quantify a given variant's impact on phenotypes such as transcription activity. Existing bioinformatics tools for Sort-seq data broadly fall into two categories: methods that model a genotype-phenotype landscape to infer latent variant phenotypes, and methods that directly estimate individual variant scores from experimental binned counts. Within this second category, sortscore provides an activity score computed directly from observed counts without fitting a model, retaining the original experimental scale when bin median values are known.We present sortscore, a python package that incorporates a standard Sort-seq scoring method and normalization across sorted samples, technical replicates from separate sort times, and across oligos in tiled experiments. It also provides convenient heatmap visualizations. This software was used to analyze DMS experiments for the transcription factor GLI2. This work seeks to lower the barrier to entry and provide a clear starting point for scoring Sort-seq cell-based functional assays. This extends the availability of well-documented and reproducible data analysis protocols to a wider community employing MAVE techniques.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The package can be downloaded from PyPI using the pip installer. The code is also freely accessible and available for reuse through a Public GitHub repository (MIT License). Installation instructions, documentation, and tutorials are accessible at the sortscore GitHub repository: https://github.com/dbaldridge-lab/sortscore. A snapshot of the code and data is available on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22119031.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary figures are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: Identifying expanding TCR clonotypes with a longitudinal Bayesian mixture model and their associations with cancer patient prognosis, metastasis-directed therapy, and VJ gene enrichment
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Examination of T cell receptor (TCR) clonality has become a way of understanding immunologic response to cancer and its interventions in recent years. An aspect of these analyses is determining which receptors expand or contract statistically significantly as a function of an exogenous perturbation such as therapeutic intervention. Results We characterize the commonly used Fisher’s exact test approach for such analyses and propose an alternative formulation that does not necessitate pairwise, within-patient comparisons. We develop this flexible Bayesian longitudinal mixture model that accommodates variable length patient followup and handles missingness where present, not omitting data in estimation because of structural practicalities. Once clones are partitioned by the model into dynamic (expanding or contracting) and static categories, one can associate their counts or other characteristics with disease state, interventions, baseline biomarkers, and patient prognosis. We apply these developments to a cohort of prostate cancer patients who underwent randomized metastasis-directed therapy or not. Our analyses reveal a significant increase in clonal expansions among metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) patients and their association with later progressions both independent and within strata of MDT. Analysis of receptor motifs and VJ gene enrichment combinations using a high-dimensional penalized log-linear model we develop also suggests distinct biological characteristics of expanding clones, with and without inducement by MDT. Availability and Implementation An example model implementation in R/STAN is available at doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21209546

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
近年来，检测T细胞受体（TCR）的克隆性已成为理解机体对癌症的免疫反应及相关干预措施效果的重要手段。这类分析的核心在于确定在某种外源性因素（如治疗干预）的作用下，哪些TCR克隆会显著增加或减少。  

**研究方法**  
我们详细探讨了目前常用的Fisher精确检验方法，并提出了一种新的分析方案，该方案无需进行患者内部的成对比较。所开发的这种灵活的贝叶斯纵向混合模型能够适应患者随访时间长度不一的情况，同时也能有效处理数据缺失问题，从而确保估计结果的可靠性。通过将该模型应用于接受或未接受转移导向治疗的前列腺癌患者队列，我们发现：接受转移导向治疗的患者中，TCR克隆的数量显著增加，且这一现象在所有治疗组中均普遍存在；进一步分析还揭示了这些扩增的TCR克隆具有独特的生物学特征。  

**结论**  
我们的研究为理解癌症免疫反应及干预措施的效果提供了新的理论工具与方法论支持。

papers.title: COBRA: Cell-type-specific Orthogonal Batch effect Removal Algorithm in single cell RNA-sequencing data
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution profiling of cellular heterogeneity, yet batch effects remain a critical challenge in data integration. Existing batch correction methods often assume homogeneous batch effect across cell types, operate in reduced-dimensional space leading to potential loss of biological information, and require extensive computational resources. Results Here, we introduce COBRA, a linear model-based batch correction method that explicitly adjusts cell-type-specific batch effect. By orthogonalizing batch-associated parameters with respect to biological variables, COBRA removes technical artifacts while preserving biologically meaningful transcriptional differences. When cell type annotations are unavailable, COBRA implements an iterative clustering algorithm to estimate pseudo-cell types while accounting for batch effects. COBRA retains the full gene expression matrix, ensuring seamless integration for downstream analyses. We evaluated COBRA across simulated and real-world datasets, including type 2 diabetes and COVID-19 datasets. COBRA outperformed in terms of batch mixing efficiency, preservation of biological group structure, and accuracy of differentially expressed gene detection. Availability COBRA is freely available at https://github.com/wonlab-healthstat/COBRA . The code to reproduce the analyses is archived at Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19891355 )

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
单细胞RNA测序技术能够高分辨率地分析细胞间的异质性，但批次效应仍然是数据整合过程中面临的关键挑战。现有的批次校正方法通常假设不同细胞类型之间的批次效应是均匀的，这些方法在降维空间中进行运算，可能导致生物信息的丢失，并且需要大量的计算资源。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了COBRA这一基于线性模型的批次校正方法，该方法能够针对不同细胞类型特异性地调整批次效应。通过将与批次相关的参数与生物学变量进行正交化处理，COBRA既去除了技术性干扰，又保留了具有生物学意义的转录差异。当缺乏细胞类型注释时，COBRA会利用迭代聚类算法来估算伪细胞类型，同时考虑批次效应的影响。由于COBRA能够保留完整的基因表达矩阵，因此它能够为后续的分析提供无缝的支持。  

我们在包括2型糖尿病和COVID-19数据集在内的多种模拟及真实数据集中对COBRA进行了评估。结果表明，COBRA在批次效应的校正效率、生物组结构的保持能力以及差异表达基因检测的准确性方面均表现优异。  

**开源情况**  
COBRA已免费开放在https://github.com/wonlab-healthstat/COBRA网站上。用于重现实验结果的代码也存储在Zenodo平台上，链接为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19891355。

all_papers.title: Identifying expanding TCR clonotypes with a longitudinal Bayesian mixture model and their associations with cancer patient prognosis, metastasis-directed therapy, and VJ gene enrichment
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Examination of T cell receptor (TCR) clonality has become a way of understanding immunologic response to cancer and its interventions in recent years. An aspect of these analyses is determining which receptors expand or contract statistically significantly as a function of an exogenous perturbation such as therapeutic intervention. Results We characterize the commonly used Fisher’s exact test approach for such analyses and propose an alternative formulation that does not necessitate pairwise, within-patient comparisons. We develop this flexible Bayesian longitudinal mixture model that accommodates variable length patient followup and handles missingness where present, not omitting data in estimation because of structural practicalities. Once clones are partitioned by the model into dynamic (expanding or contracting) and static categories, one can associate their counts or other characteristics with disease state, interventions, baseline biomarkers, and patient prognosis. We apply these developments to a cohort of prostate cancer patients who underwent randomized metastasis-directed therapy or not. Our analyses reveal a significant increase in clonal expansions among metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) patients and their association with later progressions both independent and within strata of MDT. Analysis of receptor motifs and VJ gene enrichment combinations using a high-dimensional penalized log-linear model we develop also suggests distinct biological characteristics of expanding clones, with and without inducement by MDT. Availability and Implementation An example model implementation in R/STAN is available at doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21209546

**摘要**

MOTIVATION: Examination of T cell receptor (TCR) clonality has become a way of understanding immunologic response to cancer and its interventions in recent years. An aspect of these analyses is determining which receptors expand or contract statistically significantly as a function of an exogenous perturbation such as therapeutic intervention.

RESULTS: We characterize the commonly used Fisher's exact test approach for such analyses and propose an alternative formulation that does not necessitate pairwise, within-patient comparisons. We develop this flexible Bayesian longitudinal mixture model that accommodates variable length patient followup and handles missingness where present, not omitting data in estimation because of structural practicalities. Once clones are partitioned by the model into dynamic (expanding or contracting) and static categories, one can associate their counts or other characteristics with disease state, interventions, baseline biomarkers, and patient prognosis. We apply these developments to a cohort of prostate cancer patients who underwent randomized metastasis-directed therapy or not. Our analyses reveal a significant increase in clonal expansions among metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) patients and their association with later progressions both independent and within strata of MDT. Analysis of receptor motifs and VJ gene enrichment combinations using a high-dimensional penalized log-linear model we develop also suggests distinct biological characteristics of expanding clones, with and without inducement by MDT.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: An example model implementation in R/STAN is available at doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21209546.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary material includes simulation results, longitudinal mixture model component derivation, HLA typing analysis, and stability selection for the VJ gene family.

all_papers.title: sortscore: Sort-seq MAVE scoring and visualization using Python
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary A growing number of tools enable the analysis of large variant libraries produced by multiplexed assays of variant effects (MAVEs). Experiments using fluorescent reporters and fluorescence-activated cell sorting sequencing (FACS-seq or Sort-seq) can coarsely quantify a given variant's impact on phenotypes such as transcription activity. Existing bioinformatics tools for Sort-seq data broadly fall into two categories: methods that model a genotype-phenotype landscape to infer latent variant phenotypes, and methods that directly estimate individual variant scores from experimental binned counts. Within this second category, sortscore provides an activity score computed directly from observed counts without fitting a model, retaining the original experimental scale when bin median values are known.We present sortscore, a python package that incorporates a standard Sort-seq scoring method and normalization across sorted samples, technical replicates from separate sort times, and across oligos in tiled experiments. It also provides convenient heatmap visualizations. This software was used to analyze DMS experiments for the transcription factor GLI2. This work seeks to lower the barrier to entry and provide a clear starting point for scoring Sort-seq cell-based functional assays. This extends the availability of well-documented and reproducible data analysis protocols to a wider community employing MAVE techniques. Availability and Implementation The package can be downloaded from PyPI using the pip installer. The code is also freely accessible and available for reuse through a Public GitHub repository (MIT License). Installation instructions, documentation, and tutorials are accessible at the sortscore GitHub repository: https://github.com/dbaldridge-lab/sortscore . A snapshot of the code and data is available on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22119031

llm_highlights_zh: 利用荧光报告基因及荧光激活细胞分选测序技术（FACS-seq或Sort-seq）进行的实验，能够大致量化特定变异对转录活性等表型特征的影响程度。
现有的用于处理Sort-seq数据的生物信息学工具大致可分为两类：一类是那些通过构建基因型-表型关系模型来推断潜在变异体所对应的表型特征的方法；另一类则是直接根据实验中获得的分箱计数结果来计算各个变异体的具体得分的方法。

摘要：越来越多的工具能够帮助分析通过多重测序技术产生的大量变异数据。利用荧光报告基因及荧光激活细胞分选测序技术，可以大致量化特定变异对转录活性等表型特征的影响。目前用于处理Sort-seq数据的生物信息学工具主要分为两类：一类是通过建立基因型-表型模型来推断潜在的变异效应；另一类则是直接根据实验结果计算各个变异的得分。在这第二类工具中，sortscore是一种无需建立模型即可根据观测数据直接计算变异活性的工具——当已知数据分组的中间值时，该工具能够保留原始的实验测量尺度。我们开发的sortscore是一个Python软件包，它包含了标准的Sort-seq评分方法，并能对不同时间进行的分选实验结果、重复实验数据以及嵌套实验中的多种寡核苷酸序列数据进行标准化处理；同时，它还提供了便捷的热图可视化功能。该工具已被用于分析GLI2转录因子的相关实验数据。我们的目标是降低使用Sort-seq技术进行细胞功能分析的门槛，为相关研究提供可靠的起点与方法支持，从而让更多采用多重测序技术的科研人员能够方便地利用这些经过充分验证的数据分析流程。

all_papers.title: COBRA: Cell-type-specific Orthogonal Batch effect Removal Algorithm in single cell RNA-sequencing data
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution profiling of cellular heterogeneity, yet batch effects remain a critical challenge in data integration. Existing batch correction methods often assume homogeneous batch effect across cell types, operate in reduced-dimensional space leading to potential loss of biological information, and require extensive computational resources. Results Here, we introduce COBRA, a linear model-based batch correction method that explicitly adjusts cell-type-specific batch effect. By orthogonalizing batch-associated parameters with respect to biological variables, COBRA removes technical artifacts while preserving biologically meaningful transcriptional differences. When cell type annotations are unavailable, COBRA implements an iterative clustering algorithm to estimate pseudo-cell types while accounting for batch effects. COBRA retains the full gene expression matrix, ensuring seamless integration for downstream analyses. We evaluated COBRA across simulated and real-world datasets, including type 2 diabetes and COVID-19 datasets. COBRA outperformed in terms of batch mixing efficiency, preservation of biological group structure, and accuracy of differentially expressed gene detection. Availability COBRA is freely available at https://github.com/wonlab-healthstat/COBRA . The code to reproduce the analyses is archived at Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19891355 )

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
单细胞RNA测序技术能够高分辨率地分析细胞间的异质性，但批次效应仍然是数据整合过程中面临的关键挑战。现有的批次校正方法通常假设不同细胞类型之间的批次效应是均匀的，这些方法在降维空间中进行运算，可能导致生物信息的丢失，并且需要大量的计算资源。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了COBRA这一基于线性模型的批次校正方法，该方法能够针对不同细胞类型特异性地调整批次效应。通过将与批次相关的参数与生物学变量进行正交化处理，COBRA既去除了技术性干扰，又保留了具有生物学意义的转录差异。当缺乏细胞类型注释时，COBRA会利用迭代聚类算法来估算伪细胞类型，同时考虑批次效应的影响。由于COBRA能够保留完整的基因表达矩阵，因此它能够为后续的分析提供无缝的支持。  

我们在包括2型糖尿病和COVID-19数据集在内的多种模拟及真实数据集中对COBRA进行了评估。结果表明，COBRA在批次效应的校正效率、生物组结构的保持能力以及差异表达基因检测的准确性方面均表现优异。  

**开源情况**

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution profiling of cellular heterogeneity, yet batch effects remain a critical challenge in data integration. Existing batch correction methods often assume homogeneous batch effect across cell types, operate in reduced-dimensional space leading to potential loss of biological information, and require extensive computational resources.

RESULTS: Here, we introduce COBRA, a linear model-based batch correction method that explicitly adjusts cell-type-specific batch effect. By orthogonalizing batch-associated parameters with respect to biological variables, COBRA removes technical artifacts while preserving biologically meaningful transcriptional differences. When cell type annotations are unavailable, COBRA implements an iterative clustering algorithm to estimate pseudo-cell types while accounting for batch effects. COBRA retains the full gene expression matrix, ensuring seamless integration for downstream analyses. We evaluated COBRA across simulated and real-world datasets, including type 2 diabetes and COVID-19 datasets. COBRA outperformed in terms of batch mixing efficiency, preservation of biological group structure, and accuracy of differentially expressed gene detection.

AVAILABILITY: COBRA is freely available at https://github.com/wonlab-healthstat/COBRA. The code to reproduce the analyses is archived at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19891355).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
